title: Platform systems & services: how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospectives, and roadmap
author: Priya Natarajan
summary: Centralized platform engineering reference combining systems and services inventory, operational how-tos, dashboard and alerting standards, canonical runbooks, recent retrospectives with action items, and a 12-month roadmap. Intended as the team wiki single-pane-of-glass for platform ownership and on-call handoffs.
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates platform systems & services guidance: ownership, common operational procedures, dashboard and alerting standards, runbooks for critical flows, a short set of post-incident retrospectives with concrete action items, and the team roadmap for the next 12 months. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and cross-functional partners who operate or depend on platform services.

Scope:
- Services covered: auth & RBAC, environment provisioning (Terraform), GPU fleet scheduler, API gateway, observability pipelines (prometheus/tempo/loki), metrics aggregation, alerting, and the platform control plane microservices.
- Not covered: customer-specific private deployment runbooks (see eng-private-deployments).

Owners & contacts:
- Platform systems: Platform Team (primary) — owner: Priya Natarajan (platform-systems)
- Observability & dashboards: Observability subteam — primary: Marco Li
- On-call rotation: SRE rotation roster (see runbook links)
- Escalation: Pager duty -> Platform lead -> Head of Eng (see Escalation Matrix table below)

Key components (inventory):
- control-plane-api (service) — SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime, P90 latency < 120ms
- scheduler (gpu-fleet-scheduler) — SLA: 99.5% during business hours, throughput targets by GPU type
- infra-provisioner (terraform-runner) — internal automation for onboarding infra stacks
- observability-pipeline — Prometheus -> Thanos -> Graphite-compatible export -> Tempo traces
- metrics-store (timescaledb) — retention: 90 days for raw, 365 days for rolled-up

Dashboards & Alerts (standards):
- Dashboard naming: platform.<service>.<view> (examples: platform.control-plane.summary, platform.scheduler.capacity)
- Dashboard ownership: every dashboard must list an owner in the top-right (owner: team/name and pager duty escalation)
- Minimum dashboard panels: error rate, latency heatmap, request rate, system resource usage, recent deploys, ongoing incidents
- Alerting thresholds (example defaults):
  * control-plane high error rate: service_error_rate >= 3% for 5m -> P1 alert
  * control-plane latency degradation: p95_latency >= 250ms for 5m -> P2 alert
  * scheduler low capacity: free_gpus_percent <= 10% for 2m -> P1 alert (business-hours), P2 otherwise
  * observability-ingest lag: scrape_latency_seconds >= 30s for 5m -> P2 alert
- Alert metadata must include: summary, runbook link, owner, severity, and run_time windows (business-hours vs 24x7).

Canonical dashboards (links):
- platform.control-plane.summary — owner: Marco Li — panels: errors, latency, requests, deployments
- platform.scheduler.capacity — owner: Ashwin Patel — panels: GPU utilization, queue length, preemption events
- platform.observability.ingest — owner: Aisha Thompson — panels: ingestion lag, storage pressure, write failures

Runbooks (high-level and links):
- control-plane-p1-runbook: Immediate steps
  1) Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty.
  2) Post to #platform-incident and set Slack incident channel.
  3) Check recent deploys (CI/CD) and rollback if a deploy is correlated.
  4) Validate database connectivity and circuit-breakers (command: "kubectl -n platform exec -it control-plane-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -fs localhost:8080/health'").
  5) If unable to recover in 15 minutes, escalate to Platform Lead and Open Incident Review.

- scheduler-capacity-runbook: Capacity shortage
  1) Confirm metric: free_gpus_percent and pending_pods queue length.
 2) If capacity shortage is due to noisy workloads, identify top-k pods by GPU usage and coordinate with owner to scale down.
 3) Trigger autoscaler policy: "platform-accelerator-burst" (manual CLI: plaftool autoscale trigger --policy burst --reason "oncall")
 4) If bursting fails, open a request to infra to allocate warm pool (tags: gpu-warm-pool).

- observability-ingest-runbook: Ingest lag
 1) Validate Prometheus scraping targets and scrape_duration_seconds.
 2) Restart the ingest pipeline worker: systemctl restart obs-ingest-worker or kubectl rollout restart deploy/obs-ingest
 3) If storage pressure, trigger retention-policy temporary increase: retention.set --days 7 --reason "ingest-backlog"

Runbook SLA & Playbook expectations:
- P1 incidents: page 24x7, 15m ack target, 60m resolution target for full-service recovery or mitigation fallback.
- P2 incidents: page business-hours, 60m ack target, 6h resolution target.
- Post-incident: run a retrospective within 72 hours and publish to eng-platform/team-retrospectives.

Escalation Matrix (table):
- Priority | First responder | Time to escalate | Second escalation
- P1 | On-call platform SRE | 15 minutes | Platform Lead -> Head of Engineering
- P2 | On-call platform SRE (business hours) | 60 minutes | Platform IC -> Platform Lead

Retrospectives (recent):
- Incident: 2026-01-12 control-plane flaky deploy
  * Summary: A misconfigured feature flag caused a cascading increase in DB queries which drove the control-plane CPU to saturation and GC pauses.
  * Impact: ~30 minutes partial outage for hosted API metadata endpoints; no customer data lost.
  * Root cause: missing deploy-time feature flag validation step in CI and insufficient autoscaling headroom for DB proxy.
  * Actions completed: rolled back offending deploy, increased DB proxy autoscale min replicas, added feature-flag CI validation unit test.
  * Actions planned: add pre-deploy synthetic load test in Canary workflow (owner: QA infra, ETA: 2026-03-31), increase cross-service circuit-breaker defaults (owner: Platform Services, ETA: 2026-02-28).

- Incident: 2025-10-04 scheduler capacity depletion during burst test
  * Summary: Load-driver incorrectly left in production causing queued jobs to exceed scheduler limits.
  * Actions completed: removed load-driver, rebalanced warm pool, documented autoscaling policy.
  * Actions planned: create billing-aware throttling to avoid noisy neighbor saturation (owner: CostOps, ETA: 2026-04-15).

Operational how-tos (short recipes):
- How to add a dashboard: Clone the platform.template dashboard, update metadata block (owner, description, tags), run grafana-cli dashboard push --file <json> --namespace platform, add to team folder.
- How to add an alert: Create a PrometheusRule with labels: severity, owner, runbook; test with promtool test rule.yml; merge to infra repo, and deploy via CI.
- How to onboard a service: 1) Create a service entry in platform-services.yaml (fields: service_name, owner, sla, tags). 2) Add dashboards and alerts. 3) Add SLOs to slo-registry. 4) Run safety checklist (deploy in staging, run synthetic traffic, validate observability).

Roadmap (12 months, high level):
- Q1 2026: Observability pipeline hardening — reduce ingest lag by 40%, ship trace sampling controls, and add alert deduplication. (owners: Observability team)
- Q2 2026: Scheduler improvements — dynamic bin-packing, preemption-safe eviction, and GPU warm-pool autoscaling. (owners: Scheduler team)
- Q3 2026: Control plane resilience — split read/write paths, add multi-region routing for failover. (owners: Platform Services)
- Q4 2026: Platform devex — self-serve onboarding UI for infra provisioning, policy-as-code for guardrails. (owners: Developer Experience)

Team wiki & resources (canonical links and locations):
- eng-platform/team-wiki (team handbook and rotation)
- eng-platform/platform-systems-and-services-playbook-2026 (comprehensive playbook)
- eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (SLO registry and error budgets)
- eng-infra/terraform-and-iac (infrastructure templates)
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture (runtime interactions and performance notes)

Appendix: SLO table (examples):
- service | availability | latency (p90) | alert threshold
- control-plane | 99.9% monthly | p90 < 120ms | availability < 99.7% over 24h -> page P1
- scheduler | 99.5% business hours | p90 < 400ms | free_gpus_percent < 10% for 10m -> page P1
- observability-ingest | 99.0% | ingest_lag < 30s | ingest_lag >= 30s for 5m -> page P2

Appendix: Useful commands & snippets:
- Check control-plane health: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=control-plane -o wide
- Stream control-plane logs: kubectl -n platform logs -f deploy/control-plane --since=10m
- Trigger autoscaler policy (CLI): plaftool autoscale trigger --policy burst --reason "oncall"

Maintenance windows & change policy:
- Platform maintenance windows are scheduled Sundays 02:00-06:00 UTC. Emergency maintenance may be performed outside these windows with Platform Lead approval.
- All changes must have a roll-back plan and a runbook entry. Large infra changes must go through the Platform Architecture review (see architecture-and-standards/decision-records).

Document maintenance:
- This page owner (Priya Natarajan) is responsible for quarterly updates. Post-incident retrospective summaries should be attached within 3 business days of incident closure.

References and related pages:
- See also: eng-platform/platform-systems-services-comprehensive-playbook-2026-q1, eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q2

End of document.
